title: Independent Cross-Stack Benchmark Evaluates Commercial Quantum Error Management on 156-Qubit IBM Heron Hardware - Quantum Computing Report
gist: An independent academic benchmark on IBM's 156-qubit ibm_pittsburgh Heron r3 compared native Qiskit Runtime error handling with Q-CTRL Performance Management and Qedma QESEM. Q-CTRL won every sampling test and cut expectation-value error 3.10x at baseline QPU time; Qedma cut error 4.70x but used 7.5–11.1x more QPU time than Q-CTRL.

insights.claim: Researchers from The Catholic University of America, University of Deusto, and Universidad de los Andes independently benchmarked IBM Qiskit Runtime primitives against third-party Qiskit Functions Catalog pipelines (Q-CTRL Performance Management and Qedma QESEM) on ibm_pittsburgh, a 156-qubit IBM Heron r3 processor.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Independent (non-vendor) comparisons of error-management stacks are rare and can shift enterprise buying decisions within IBM's ecosystem.
insights.locator: An independent benchmarking study published on arXiv

insights.claim: In the benchmark, IBM and Q-CTRL ran under matched shot budgets of 32,768 shots per instance, while Qedma QESEM used its native precision-and-time interface (0.1 precision target, 600-second QPU cap), with all workloads submitted in identical calibration windows.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Qedma's different budgeting model means its results trade cost for accuracy; comparisons should be read on an accuracy-per-QPU-second basis.
insights.locator: The benchmark evaluates two execution models

insights.claim: Across Bernstein–Vazirani, Quantum Phase Estimation, GHZ-state preparation, and Randomized Mirror Circuits (25–100 qubits), Q-CTRL's autonomous error-suppression pipeline delivered the highest exact-output success probability in all 12 sampling test cases.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A clean sweep in an independent benchmark strengthens Q-CTRL's commercial case as the default error-suppression layer on IBM hardware.
insights.quote: Q-CTRL’s autonomous suppression pipeline delivered the highest exact-output success probabilities across all 12 test cases

insights.claim: On 30-qubit Quantum Phase Estimation, raw and measurement-twirled IBM runs produced zero exact-match shots out of 32,768, while Q-CTRL achieved a 12.69% exact success probability.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Error suppression software can decide whether an algorithm works at all on current hardware, not just improve it marginally.

insights.claim: On 100-qubit Randomized Mirror Circuits, Q-CTRL kept a 76.45% exact target-string success rate compared with 9.14% for raw IBM execution.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An ~8x improvement at 100 qubits shows software layers materially extend the useful scale of existing IBM processors.

themes.theme: Estimator track: accuracy vs. QPU cost

insights.claim: On an eight-layer Transverse-Field Ising Model circuit at 25–75 qubits, overall mean absolute error versus an exact MPS reference was 0.0883 for raw IBM, 0.0807 for IBM TREX plus twirling (1.09x reduction), 0.0285 for Q-CTRL (3.10x), and 0.0188 for Qedma QESEM (4.70x).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IBM's own built-in mitigation barely beats raw execution, leaving a large gap that third-party vendors are monetizing.
insights.locator: Estimator Track Accuracy & QPU Overhead Benchmarks

insights.claim: Q-CTRL achieved its 3.10x error reduction using about 28 seconds of QPU time per job, in line with IBM's mitigated runs, whereas Qedma QESEM's higher 4.70x precision consumed 211–311 seconds per job, 7.5x to 11.1x Q-CTRL's runtime.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Because QPU time is billed, error-management vendors split into a low-overhead suppression tier (Q-CTRL) and a high-precision, high-cost mitigation tier (Qedma); users will choose based on accuracy-per-dollar.

insights.claim: IBM's TREX plus gate twirling lowered magnetization error but raised correlator error (cZZ MAE 0.0587 vs 0.0282 raw) while increasing QPU time to about 28.0–37.8 seconds per job from about 17.8 seconds raw.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Native IBM resilience settings can degrade some observables at higher cost, a signal that default mitigation is not a safe choice for all workloads.
insights.locator: Estimator Track Accuracy & QPU Overhead Benchmarks
